newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco ruling boosts Florida case, governor says.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco ruling boosts Florida case, governor says.

text.p: Florida's lawsuit against the tobacco companies was significantly strengthened by an appeals court ruling allowing the state to use internal tobacco company documents as evidence, Gov. Lawton Chiles said Wednesday.

"These documents are among the most explosive in the history of the fight for tobacco justice," Chiles said. "This ruling is a devastating blow to the cigarette giants and puts a powerful wind in our sails as we move toward trial in August."
Jury selection is scheduled to begin Aug. 1 in the Florida lawsuit seeking to recover the public cost of treating tobacco-related illness.

"These documents will provide our citizens with an inside look at how the cigarette cartel has committed fraud by working to addict our children, hide the evidence and stick taxpayers with the bill," Chiles alleged.
Earlier Wednesday, Florida's 4th District Court of Appeal on upheld a ruling allowing the state to use 13 documents obtained from Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group.
The documents include memos on trial strategy, a 1964 consumer survey, a 1966 letter on the status of special company projects and a 1978 letter about carbon monoxide analysis.

The tobacco companies had argued that the documents were protected by attorney-client privilege. But the appeals court found the documents were exempt from that privilege because they involved alleged plans to commit a crime or fraud.

The appeals court noted that a special master had reviewed the documents and "found that there was evidence that the defendants hid from and misrepresented to the public the health risks of smoking and that their conduct constituted a fraud on the public."

Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth said the documents "will help us tremendously. The lives cost by this shameful deception cannot be reclaimed," he said Wednesday. "However, by holding the tobacco industry responsible for its actions, we can help prevent such tragedy in the future."
